title: Three Months and One Short Page
subtitle: 文化遗产 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：zero　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 zero 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the writer ① marked the zero that no reader in the study would have counted, and he said the marking was the whole of the month. The ② zero, meaning the number itself and not the page, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a zero, he said, is the only thing in a study that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ zero in that study had the same short page beside it, and the ④ zero at the far shelf, meaning the draft they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A zero, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the writer said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the zero was the whole of the matter, meaning the beginning and not the number. The ⑥ zero, meaning the beginning and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; zero, he said, is either something you mark or the only word that means both a number and a beginning. He said the beginning is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ zero had become a line in a manuscript, and the manuscript had become an argument about the short page. The ⑧ zero of the whole thing, the writer wrote in January, was one study and three months of counting; zero, he said, is either the draft at the far shelf or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ zero I remember is the number counted in the manuscript, which closed in 1963 and is still counted as the quietest in the study. A ⑩ zero, my mother said in 1965, is the only number that improves by being counted; every zero, she said, is a beginning that has agreed to look like a number. She said the beginning was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 零；起点（指书斋里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 零；起点（指那个零本身，与薄薄的书页相对）
C. 固定搭配：mark the zero 标出这一个零
D. n. 零；起点（指留给孩子们誊的那一份）
E. n. 零之事（抽象总称，指一处书斋的零之事）
F. n. 零；起点（指手稿里写到、被清点的那一个）
G. n. 零、一个起点（指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 一个起点（抽象总称，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: mark the zero 意为“标出这一个零”，1956 年那位写作者把书斋里没有一位读者肯清点的一个零做了一遍。
zero 意为“零；起点”，指那个零本身而不是薄薄的书页，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
zero 意为“零；起点”，指书斋里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一页薄薄的书页。
zero 意为“零；起点”，指最远那层书架的留给孩子们誊的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
zero 意为“零、一个起点”，指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个一个起点就是那件事的全部。
zero 意为“一个起点”，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个零，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
zero 意为“零；起点”，指手稿里写到、被清点的那一个，到 1961 年这一个成了手稿里的一行。
zero 意为“零之事”，写作者一月写道，整件事的零之事是一处书斋和三个月份的清点。
zero 意为“零；起点”，我记得的是手稿里清点过的那一个，1963 年写就了，至今仍被说成书斋里最安静的一个。
zero 为抽象总称，母亲 1965 年说，零是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的零。
